chapter: Reels 1-2: Roy Brown, clubs and Sam Cooke
title: Turning down a move to Los Angeles after Cooke's death
summary: He knew studio musicians in LA, including Earl Palmer, but chose to return home to his family in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Just, I mean, you know, just living, uh, because I knew a lot of the musicians. Right. And I mean, this was on bass for Sam. We used to go, be in Los Angeles. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. the way he was living at the time. And after you got killed. And you know you'd meet the musicians and say, hey man, you're going back to New Orleans? Yeah. We'll stay here, blah, blah, blah. I said, no. Well, my family was here.
And what if they said you know there was a guaranteed work for them?

Well, the them said, so you know the time you knew them the guys in the studio. I guess you would have to pay some dues, not that every door would have been open for you. Like I said, I was pretty established. I knew a lot of the studio musicians around in Earl Palmer with a very dear friend. Excuse me. So I mean, that would have been all right, but I would have had to pay some dues. But this is home.
Did you consider making the new debt?

No, well, I would have had to move my family. I had to take this under consideration. You know, see my kids were smaller at the time, and that would have been moving and giving up one thing to that. But this New Orleans is home. You know, I like that.
